FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Agriculture and Food Processing Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and 
Agriculture Division Council. 


With the ongoing modernization of rice milling system, rubber roll type paddy dehuskers are being extensively 
used throughout the country. For providing uniform guidelines for testing the rubber roll type dehusker, a need 
was felt to prepare this standard. 


This standard was originally published in 1979 and revised in 1989. In this revision, specific clauses in the 
specification sheet related to provisions for Cooling Arrangements and provision for adjusting clearance between 
rollers has been updated as per the latest industrial performance requirements. Further, a new clause related to 
dimensions of rubber roll has been incorporated in the specification sheet. Also, the standard has been brought 
out in the latest style and format of the Indian Standards. 


The composition of the committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is listed in Annex K. 


In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or 
calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical 
values (second revision)’. 


IS 9049 : 2023 


Indian Standard 


AGRICULTURAL PRODUCE MILLING MACHINER Y— PADDY 
DEHUSKER, RUBBER ROLL TYPE — TEST CODE 


( Second Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the methods for testing of 
rubber roll type paddy dehuskers to evaluate their 
performance. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards given below below contain provisions 
which, through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of 
publication, the editions indicated were valid. All 
standards are subject to revision and parties to 
agreements based on this standard are encouraged to 
investigate the possibility of applying the most 
recent editions of these standards: 


IS No. Title 


IS 4333 Methods of analysis for 
foodgrains: 


(Part 1): 2018  Refractions (third revision) 


(Part 2): 2017/ Determination of moisture 
ISO 712: 2009 content (second revision) 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


3.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following 
definitions shall apply. 


3.1 Broken Rice — Rice kernels which are broken 
and whose length is less than three-fourth of the 
original length. 


3.2 Head Rice — Rice grains of size three-fourth 
and above in length, of a whole rice grain. 


3.3 Brown Rice — Paddy from which husk only has 
been removed. It is also known as dehusked rice or 
brown rice. 


3.4 Cleaned Paddy — Paddy mass having foreign 
matter not exceeding 0.5 percent by mass. 


3.5 Feed Mechanism — A device to regulate the 
flow of paddy into the dehusker. 


3.6 Feed Rate — Mass of cleaned paddy fed into 
dehusker per unit of time. 


3.7 Foreign Matter — It includes inorganic and 
organic matters. The inorganic matter shall include 
sand, gravel, dirt, pebbles, stones, lumps of earth, 
mud and iron chips. The organic matter shall include 
chaff, straw, weed seeds, animal excreta, dead 
insects and worms and other grains. 


3.8 Paddy Dehusker — A machine used for 
removing the husk from paddy mass. 


3.9 Rated Capacity — The feed rate at which the 
shelling efficiency is 90 percent for raw paddy and 
95 percent for parboiled paddy. 


3.10 Shelled Paddy — The material coming out 
from the dehusker other than husk and impurities. 


3.11 Shelling Efficiency — This gives an indication 
of the efficiency of the dehusker and is calculated as 
follows: 


A=[ ¿x(1-D?)] x 100 


where 
A = shelling efficiency in percentage; 
B = Shelling efficiency in percentage; 
C = percentage of mass of brown rice 
present in paddy mass; and 
D = fraction of broken rice present in 


brown rice. 


4 SELECTION AND SPECIFICATION OF 
DEHUSKER 


4.1 Selection 


The paddy dehusker shall be selected at random by 
the testing authority from the production line with 
the agreement of the manufacturer. 


4.2 Specification 


The manufacturer shall supply the specification 
sheet duly filled in as given in Annex A. The 
manufacturer shall also supply all literature, 
operation and maintenance manual and spare parts 


IS 9049 : 2023 


catalogue of the dehusker. 
5 TEST 
5.1 General 
5.2 Test at No-Load (see 8) 
5.3 Tests at Load (see 9) 
a) Visual observations, 


b) Determination of: 


1) Shelling efficiency; 

2) Percentage of broken rice; 

3) Percentage of unshelled paddy; 
4) Percentage of husk; 

5) Rated capacity; 

6) Power consumption; and 

7) Aspiration efficiency. 


5.4 Long-Run Tests (see 10) 
6 PRE-TEST OBSERVATIONS 
6.1 Determination of Foreign Matter 


The presence of foreign matter in the cleaned paddy 
shall be determined in accordance with 4, 5 and 6.2 
of IS 4333 (Part 1). 


6.2 Determination of Moisture 


The moisture content of the cleaned paddy shall be 
determined in accordance with IS 4333 (Part 2). 


6.3 Determination of Rice Husk Ratio 


Five samples of cleaned paddy each weighing 50 g 
shall be taken. The husk from paddy shall be 
separated manually for each sample. The mass of 
husk and rice shall be taken separately for each 
sample and their ratio shall be calculated. The 
average of 5 samples shall be taken as rice-husk 
ratio. 


6.4 Running-In and Preliminary Adjustments 


6.4.1 The paddy dehusker shall be installed at level 
and preferably on firm surface. All the adjustments 
shall be made in accordance with the manufacturer’s 
recommendations. 


6.4.2 The paddy dehusker shall be attached with a 
suitable prime mover preferably with electric motor 
and auto voltage stabilizer. The energy meter or 
some form of transmission dynamometer may be 


fitted. The power delivery to the dehusker may be 
supplied in the following ways: 


a) Connecting the prime mover with the main 
shaft of the dehusker by means of flat belt 
and pulley or V-belt and pulley. 


b) Connecting the prime mover with the 
dehusker by means of V-belt running over 
V-pulley on prime mover and flat pulley on 
main shaft of the dehusker. 


6.4.2.1 In case of 6.4.2 (a), the allowances for flat 
and V-belt drive losses may be taken as 6 percent 
and 3 percent respectively, whereas in case of 6.4.2 
(b), the allowances for drive losses may be taken as 
4.5 percent. 


6.4.3 The paddy dehusker shall be run-in for atleast 
30 minutes without load before commencing the 
test. The running-in shall be carried out in 


accordance with the manufacturer’s 
recommendations. 
7 GENERAL 


7.1 Checking of Specifications 


The specifications given by the manufacturer 
(see 4.2) shall be checked and reported in the 
proforma listed in Annex A. 


7.2 Checking of Material 


The material of construction of the various 
components of the paddy dehusker shall be reported 
in the data sheet listed in Annex B. 


73 Visual Observations and Checking of 
Provisions for Adjustments 


The observations and adjustments listed in datasheet 
in Annex C shall be made and reported. 


8 TEST AT NO-LOAD 


After the running-in is over, the dehusker shall be 
run at no-load for minimum of 10 minutes at the 
rated speed. During and after no-load run, the visual 
observations given in Annex D shall be recorded. 


9 TEST AT LOAD 
9.1 Quality of Paddy 


Sufficient quantity of cleaned paddy of the same 
variety having 14 percent + 0.5 percent moisture 
content on wet basis (w.b.) shall be taken for starting 
the test. 


9.2 Operation and Collection of Data 


After the stabilization of the operation, the dehusker 
shall be operated at the speed specified for both 
rubber rolls of half an hour at the rated capacity 
specified by the manufacturer. 


9.2.1 During the above run, the following data and 
samples shall be collected: 


a) Six samples of shelled rice at an interval of 
5 minutes from rice outlet and husk from 
husk outlet; 


b) The speed of the both rubber rolls of the 
dehusker in revolutions per minute; and 


c) The energy meter reading at an interval of 
5 minutes in kWh. 


9.2.2 At the end of half an hour feeding, run the 
dehusker idle for some time so that practically no 
material already fed comes out. At the end of the 
test, collect and weigh the shelled paddy received at 
the main grain outlet. The mass of the sample 
collected at main grain outlet [see 9.2.1 (a)] shall be 
added to the mass of the shelled paddy collected 
after the run test. During and after run test, inspect 
the dehusker visually. 


9.2.3 The tests given in 9.2, 9.2.1 and 9.2.2 shall be 
repeated with the feed rates 80 percent, 90 percent, 
110 percent, 120 percent of the rated capacity 
declared by the manufacturer. 


9.2.4 The data shall be recorded in the datasheet as 
listed in Annex E. 


NOTE — For the purpose of certification, the dehusker 
shall be operated only at rated feed rate and test at 9.2.3 need 
not be conducted. 


9.3 Preparation and Analysis of Samples 


The six sets of the samples obtained [see 9.2.1 (a)] 
for various feed rates shall be thoroughly mixed 
separately to form a composite sample for each feed 
rate. Out of each composite sample, 100 g of sample 
shall be taken and analysed for the following: 


a) Presence of husk; 
b) Presence of unshelled paddy; and 
c) Presence of broken rice. 


9.3.1 The data shall be recorded in the datasheet as 
listed in Annex F. 


9.4 Calculations 


From the observations made above, the following

shall be calculated: 


B

9.4.1 The data shall be recorded in data sheet as 
listed in Annex G. 


9.5 Determination of Rated Capacity 


From the load tests described earlier, select the 
maximum feed rate at which the shelling efficiency 
is not less than 90 percent for raw paddy and 
95 percent for parboiled paddy. This feed rate shall 
be taken as the rated capacity. The data shall be 
recorded in data sheet as listed in Annex G. 


9.6 Determination of Power Consumption 
The difference between the two consecutive energy 


meter readings [see 9.2.1 (c)] shall be taken as the 
energy consumption for 5 minutes. 


The power consumption shall be calculated giving 
due allowance to the type of drive (see 6.4.2.1). The 
data shall be recorded in the data sheet listed in 
Annex G. 


10 LONG RUN TEST 


10.1 The dehusker shall be operated for a minimum 
period of 20 hours at no load. This period should be 
covered in a maximum of 4 continuous runs. During 
and after the operation, no breakdown or defect shall 
develop in the dehusker. 


10.1.1 The major breakdowns, defect developed and 
repairs made during the run period shall be recorded 
in the data sheet listed in Annex H. 


11 SUMMARY REPORT 


11.1 For the guidance of the user, compile a 
summary report on the proforma as given in 
Annex J. 


IS 9049 : 2023

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: FAD 20 (20845).
